subject: physics
question: A car starts from rest and accelerates uniformly at $2\ \text{m/s}^2$. Its speed after $5$ s is

subject: physics
question: A car starts from rest with constant acceleration $2\ \text{m/s}^2$. The distance it travels in the first $5$ s is
explanation: $x=v_0t+\tfrac12at^2=0+\tfrac12\times2\times5^2=25$ m.

subject: physics
question: A stone is dropped from rest and falls freely for $3$ s (take $g=10\ \text{m/s}^2$). The distance fallen is
explanation: $h=\tfrac12gt^2=\tfrac12\times10\times9=45$ m.

subject: physics
question: A ball is thrown vertically upward at $20$ m/s (take $g=10\ \text{m/s}^2$). The maximum height it reaches is
explanation: At the top $v=0$: $v_0^2=2gh\Rightarrow h=\dfrac{v_0^2}{2g}=\dfrac{400}{20}=20$ m.

subject: physics
question: A car moving at $20$ m/s brakes with a deceleration of $5\ \text{m/s}^2$. The distance it travels in the $6$ s after braking starts is
explanation:
The car stops after $t=\dfrac{20}{5}=4$ s, so it does **not** move during the last $2$ s.

Stopping distance: $\dfrac{v_0^2}{2a}=\dfrac{400}{10}=40$ m. (Using $t=6$ s in $x=v_0t-\tfrac12at^2$ gives $30$ m — the classic trap.)

subject: physics
question: An object moves $30$ m east and then $40$ m north in $10$ s. The magnitude of its average velocity is
explanation: Average velocity $=\dfrac{\text{displacement}}{\text{time}}$. Displacement $=\sqrt{30^2+40^2}=50$ m, so $\bar v=5$ m/s. ($7$ m/s is the average **speed**, from the path length $70$ m.)

subject: physics
question: An object accelerates uniformly from $2$ m/s to $10$ m/s over a distance of $24$ m. Its acceleration is
explanation: $v^2-v_0^2=2ax\Rightarrow a=\dfrac{100-4}{2\times24}=2\ \text{m/s}^2$.

subject: physics
question: A ball is thrown horizontally at $10$ m/s from a height of $20$ m (take $g=10\ \text{m/s}^2$). The horizontal distance it travels before hitting the ground is
explanation: Vertical motion is free fall: $20=\tfrac12\cdot10\,t^2\Rightarrow t=2$ s. Horizontal motion is uniform: $x=v_0t=10\times2=20$ m.

subject: physics
question: For the projectile in the previous situation (thrown horizontally at $10$ m/s from $20$ m, $g=10\ \text{m/s}^2$), the speed when it hits the ground is
explanation: After $t=2$ s: $v_y=gt=20$ m/s, $v_x=10$ m/s. $v=\sqrt{10^2+20^2}=10\sqrt5\approx22.4$ m/s. Speeds add as vectors, not as numbers.

subject: physics
question: On a velocity–time graph, the area between the graph and the time axis represents
explanation: Displacement $=\int v\,dt$, which is the area under the $v$–$t$ graph. The **slope** of the $v$–$t$ graph is the acceleration.

subject: physics
question: An object starting from rest moves with uniform acceleration. The ratio of the distances covered in the 1st, 2nd and 3rd seconds is
explanation: Total distances after $1,2,3$ s are proportional to $1,4,9$ (since $x\propto t^2$). Distances **in each** second: $1,\ 4-1=3,\ 9-4=5$, ratio $1:3:5$.

subject: physics
question: Two cars start together from the same place along a straight road. Car A moves at a constant $10$ m/s; car B starts from rest with acceleration $2\ \text{m/s}^2$. The maximum distance between them before B catches up is
explanation:
The gap grows while A is faster and shrinks once B is faster, so it is greatest when the speeds are equal: $2t=10$, $t=5$ s.

Gap $=10\times5-\tfrac12\times2\times5^2=50-25=25$ m.

subject: physics
question: A stone is dropped from the top of a tower and takes $4$ s to reach the ground (take $g=10\ \text{m/s}^2$). The distance it falls during the last second is
explanation: In $4$ s: $\tfrac12\cdot10\cdot16=80$ m. In $3$ s: $\tfrac12\cdot10\cdot9=45$ m. Last second: $80-45=35$ m.

subject: physics
question: A ball is thrown upward from the ground at $15$ m/s (take $g=10\ \text{m/s}^2$). At what times is it $10$ m above the ground?
explanation: $10=15t-5t^2\Rightarrow t^2-3t+2=0\Rightarrow t=1$ s (on the way up) or $t=2$ s (on the way down). Both are valid because the ball rises to $\dfrac{15^2}{20}=11.25$ m $>10$ m.

subject: physics
question: A net force of $12$ N acts on a $3$ kg block. Its acceleration is
explanation: Newton's second law: $a=\dfrac{F}{m}=\dfrac{12}{3}=4\ \text{m/s}^2$.

subject: physics
question: A book rests on a table. The reaction force (Newton's third law partner) to the gravitational force of the Earth on the book is
options: the gravitational force of the book on the Earth
the normal force of the table on the book
the force of the book on the table
the friction force on the book
explanation: Third-law pairs act on **different** bodies and are of the same type. The Earth pulls the book down by gravity, so the book pulls the Earth up by gravity. The normal force balances the weight, but it is a different interaction (first-law balance, not a third-law pair).

subject: physics
question: A $2$ kg block is pulled along a horizontal floor by a horizontal force of $10$ N. The coefficient of kinetic friction is $0.3$ (take $g=10\ \text{m/s}^2$). The acceleration of the block is
explanation: Friction $f=\mu mg=0.3\times2\times10=6$ N. Net force $=10-6=4$ N, so $a=\dfrac42=2\ \text{m/s}^2$.

subject: physics
question: A block slides down a smooth (frictionless) incline of angle $30^\circ$ (take $g=10\ \text{m/s}^2$). Its acceleration is
explanation: Only the component of gravity along the slope accelerates the block: $a=g\sin30^\circ=10\times\tfrac12=5\ \text{m/s}^2$. The mass cancels.

subject: physics
question: A person of mass $50$ kg stands on a scale in a lift that accelerates **upward** at $2\ \text{m/s}^2$ (take $g=10\ \text{m/s}^2$). The scale reads
explanation: $N-mg=ma\Rightarrow N=m(g+a)=50\times12=600$ N. The person feels heavier (overweight).

subject: physics
question: Blocks of mass $2$ kg and $3$ kg are in contact on a smooth horizontal surface. A horizontal force of $10$ N pushes the $2$ kg block, which pushes the $3$ kg block. The force between the blocks is
explanation: Whole system: $a=\dfrac{10}{2+3}=2\ \text{m/s}^2$. The $3$ kg block is accelerated only by the contact force: $F_{12}=3\times2=6$ N.

subject: physics
question: A passenger in a bus that suddenly brakes lurches forward. This is best explained by
options: a forward force acting on the passenger
explanation: The passenger's body tends to keep moving at the original speed (inertia) while the bus slows down. No forward force pushes the passenger.

subject: physics
question: Two forces of $3$ N and $4$ N act on an object at right angles. The magnitude of the resultant force is
explanation: Perpendicular forces add like the sides of a right triangle: $F=\sqrt{3^2+4^2}=5$ N.

subject: physics
question: A $10$ kg box rests on a horizontal floor with static friction coefficient $0.5$ (take $g=10\ \text{m/s}^2$). A horizontal push of $30$ N is applied. The friction force on the box is
explanation: Maximum static friction $=\mu_sN=0.5\times100=50$ N. The push $30$ N is smaller, so the box does not move and static friction just balances the push: $f=30$ N.

subject: physics
question: An object of weight $20$ N hangs from two strings, each making an angle of $60^\circ$ with the vertical. The tension in each string is
explanation: Vertical equilibrium: $2T\cos60^\circ=20\Rightarrow T=\dfrac{20}{2\times\frac12}=20$ N.

subject: physics
question: The SI unit of force, the newton, is equivalent to
explanation: From $F=ma$: $1\ \text{N}=1\ \text{kg}\times1\ \text{m/s}^2$. ($\text{kg}\cdot\text{m/s}$ is momentum and $\text{kg}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{s}^2$ is energy.)

subject: physics
question: Masses of $3$ kg and $2$ kg hang from the two ends of a light string over a light, frictionless pulley (take $g=10\ \text{m/s}^2$). The acceleration of the masses is
explanation: Net driving force $=(3-2)g=10$ N; total mass $=5$ kg. $a=\dfrac{10}{5}=2\ \text{m/s}^2$.

subject: physics
question: A block slides down an incline of angle $37^\circ$ with kinetic friction coefficient $0.5$ (take $g=10\ \text{m/s}^2$) and $\sin37^\circ=0.6$, $\cos37^\circ=0.8$. Its acceleration is
explanation: $a=g\sin\theta-\mu g\cos\theta=10\times0.6-0.5\times10\times0.8=6-4=2\ \text{m/s}^2$.

subject: physics
question: An object moves at constant velocity. Which statement must be true?
options: A constant force acts in the direction of motion
The net force on it is zero
explanation: Constant velocity means zero acceleration, so by Newton's first/second law the **net** force is zero. Several forces may act, but they balance.

subject: physics
question: The momentum of a $2$ kg ball moving at $3$ m/s is
explanation: $p=mv=2\times3=6\ \text{kg}\cdot\text{m/s}$. ($9$ J would be the kinetic energy $\tfrac12mv^2$.)

subject: physics
question: A constant force of $5$ N acts on an object for $4$ s. The impulse of the force is
explanation: $I=Ft=5\times4=20\ \text{N}\cdot\text{s}$.

subject: physics
question: A $0.5$ kg ball hits a wall at $6$ m/s and rebounds along the same line at $4$ m/s. The magnitude of the change in its momentum is
explanation: Take the rebound direction as positive: $\Delta p=0.5\times4-0.5\times(-6)=2+3=5\ \text{kg}\cdot\text{m/s}$. Forgetting that velocity reverses gives $1$.

subject: physics
question: A $2$ kg cart moving at $3$ m/s collides with a stationary $1$ kg cart and they stick together. Their common speed is
explanation: Momentum is conserved: $2\times3=(2+1)v\Rightarrow v=2$ m/s.

subject: physics
question: In the collision above ($2$ kg at $3$ m/s sticking to a stationary $1$ kg cart), the kinetic energy lost is
explanation: Before: $\tfrac12\times2\times9=9$ J. After: $\tfrac12\times3\times2^2=6$ J. Lost: $3$ J — a perfectly inelastic collision always loses kinetic energy.

subject: physics
question: A $60$ kg person standing on smooth ice throws a $2$ kg ball horizontally at $15$ m/s. The person's recoil speed is
explanation: Initial momentum is zero, so $60v=2\times15\Rightarrow v=0.5$ m/s, in the opposite direction.

subject: physics
question: An egg dropped onto a cushion is less likely to break than one dropped onto a stone floor because the cushion
options: increases the time of impact, reducing the force
explanation: The change in momentum (and so the impulse) is the same either way. The cushion stretches the stopping time, so $F=\dfrac{\Delta p}{\Delta t}$ is smaller.

subject: physics
question: A $1000$ kg car's speed increases from $10$ m/s to $20$ m/s in $5$ s. The average net force on it is
explanation: Impulse–momentum theorem: $F\Delta t=\Delta p=1000\times(20-10)$, so $F=\dfrac{10000}{5}=2000$ N.

subject: physics
question: A ball of mass $m$ moving at $4$ m/s makes a perfectly **elastic** head-on collision with an identical stationary ball. Afterwards the first ball's speed is
explanation: Conserving momentum and kinetic energy for equal masses gives an exchange of velocities: the first ball stops ($0$ m/s) and the second moves off at $4$ m/s.

subject: physics
question: Momentum of a system is conserved when
options: there is no friction inside the system
the net external force on the system is zero
explanation: Conservation of momentum requires zero net **external** force. Internal forces (including friction between parts of the system) cannot change the total momentum. Kinetic energy may or may not be conserved.

subject: physics
question: A $0.2$ kg ball falls from rest for $2$ s (take $g=10\ \text{m/s}^2$). The impulse of gravity on the ball during this time is
explanation: $I=mgt=0.2\times10\times2=4\ \text{N}\cdot\text{s}$, equal to the momentum gained: $0.2\times20=4\ \text{kg}\cdot\text{m/s}$.

subject: physics
question: A $3$ kg object at rest explodes into two pieces. A $1$ kg piece flies off at $8$ m/s. The speed of the other piece is
explanation: Total momentum stays zero: $1\times8=2\times v\Rightarrow v=4$ m/s in the opposite direction. (The other piece has mass $3-1=2$ kg, not $3$ kg.)

subject: physics
question: A force of $10$ N pulls a box $5$ m along the floor. The force makes an angle of $60^\circ$ with the displacement. The work done by the force is
explanation: $W=Fs\cos\theta=10\times5\times\cos60^\circ=25$ J.

subject: physics
question: The kinetic energy of a $4$ kg object moving at $5$ m/s is
explanation: $E_k=\tfrac12mv^2=\tfrac12\times4\times25=50$ J.

subject: physics
question: A $2$ kg object is lifted $3$ m vertically at constant speed (take $g=10\ \text{m/s}^2$). The increase in its gravitational potential energy is
explanation: $\Delta E_p=mgh=2\times10\times3=60$ J.

subject: physics
question: A ball is released from rest and slides down a smooth curved track, dropping a vertical height of $5$ m (take $g=10\ \text{m/s}^2$). Its speed at the bottom is
explanation: No friction, so mechanical energy is conserved: $mgh=\tfrac12mv^2\Rightarrow v=\sqrt{2gh}=\sqrt{100}=10$ m/s. The shape of the track does not matter.

subject: physics
question: A motor lifts a $50$ kg load through $12$ m in $10$ s at constant speed (take $g=10\ \text{m/s}^2$). The power output of the motor is
explanation: Work $=mgh=50\times10\times12=6000$ J; power $P=\dfrac Wt=\dfrac{6000}{10}=600$ W.

subject: physics
question: A car's engine delivers a constant power of $60$ kW. When the car moves at $20$ m/s, the driving force is
explanation: $P=Fv\Rightarrow F=\dfrac{60000}{20}=3000$ N.

subject: physics
question: A $2$ kg block sliding at $6$ m/s on a rough horizontal floor stops after $9$ m. The friction force is
explanation: Work–energy theorem: $-f\cdot9=0-\tfrac12\times2\times36=-36$ J, so $f=4$ N.

subject: physics
question: A $1$ kg ball is thrown upward from the ground at $20$ m/s and reaches a maximum height of $16$ m (take $g=10\ \text{m/s}^2$). The work done against air resistance on the way up is
explanation: Initial kinetic energy $=\tfrac12\times1\times400=200$ J. At the top it has potential energy $mgh=160$ J. The missing $40$ J was done against air resistance.

subject: physics
question: A satellite moves in a circular orbit around the Earth. The work done by gravity on it during one revolution is
options: zero, because gravity is perpendicular to the velocity
explanation: In a circular orbit the gravitational force always points to the centre, perpendicular to the velocity, so $W=Fs\cos90^\circ=0$ at every instant. The speed stays constant.

subject: physics
question: A spring with spring constant $200$ N/m is compressed by $0.1$ m. The elastic potential energy stored is
explanation: $E_p=\tfrac12kx^2=\tfrac12\times200\times0.01=1$ J.

subject: physics
question: A pendulum bob is released from rest $0.45$ m above its lowest point (take $g=10\ \text{m/s}^2$). Its speed at the lowest point is
explanation: $\tfrac12mv^2=mgh\Rightarrow v=\sqrt{2\times10\times0.45}=\sqrt9=3$ m/s. The string tension does no work (it is perpendicular to the motion).

subject: physics
question: Which quantity is a scalar?
explanation: Work $W=\vec F\cdot\vec s$ is a dot product, so it has magnitude (and sign) but no direction. Momentum, force and displacement are vectors.

subject: physics
question: A $1500$ kg car has maximum engine power $60$ kW and the total resistance is a constant $2000$ N. Its maximum speed on a level road is
explanation: At maximum speed the acceleration is zero, so the driving force equals the resistance: $F=2000$ N. $v_{\max}=\dfrac{P}{F}=\dfrac{60000}{2000}=30$ m/s.

subject: physics
question: A $2$ kg block is released from rest at the top of a $5$ m high, $10$ m long incline and reaches the bottom at $8$ m/s (take $g=10\ \text{m/s}^2$). The work done by friction is
explanation: $W_g+W_f=\Delta E_k$: $2\times10\times5+W_f=\tfrac12\times2\times64$, so $W_f=64-100=-36$ J (negative because friction opposes motion).

subject: physics
question: An object moves in a circle of radius $2$ m at a constant speed of $4$ m/s. Its centripetal acceleration is
explanation: $a=\dfrac{v^2}{r}=\dfrac{16}{2}=8\ \text{m/s}^2$, directed toward the centre. The speed is constant but the velocity's direction changes, so $a\ne0$.

subject: physics
question: A wheel turns at $2$ revolutions per second. Its angular velocity is
explanation: $\omega=2\pi n=2\pi\times2=4\pi$ rad/s.

subject: physics
question: A $0.5$ kg ball on a string moves in a horizontal circle of radius $0.4$ m on a smooth table at $2$ m/s. The tension in the string is
explanation: The tension provides the centripetal force: $T=\dfrac{mv^2}{r}=\dfrac{0.5\times4}{0.4}=5$ N.

subject: physics
question: A car of mass $1000$ kg drives over the top of a hump of radius $40$ m at $10$ m/s (take $g=10\ \text{m/s}^2$). The normal force from the road at the top is
explanation: At the top the net force points down to the centre: $mg-N=\dfrac{mv^2}{r}$, so $N=1000\left(10-\dfrac{100}{40}\right)=7500$ N. The car feels lighter.

subject: physics
question: A small ball on a string of length $0.4$ m moves in a vertical circle (take $g=10\ \text{m/s}^2$). The minimum speed at the top for the string to stay taut is
explanation: At the minimum speed the tension is zero and gravity alone gives the centripetal force: $mg=\dfrac{mv^2}r\Rightarrow v=\sqrt{gr}=\sqrt{4}=2$ m/s.

subject: physics
question: If the distance between two point masses is doubled, the gravitational force between them becomes
explanation: $F=\dfrac{Gm_1m_2}{r^2}$: doubling $r$ divides $F$ by $2^2=4$.

subject: physics
question: For satellites in circular orbits around the Earth, a satellite in a **higher** orbit has
options: a smaller speed and a longer period
a larger speed and a longer period
a smaller speed and a shorter period
explanation: $\dfrac{GMm}{r^2}=\dfrac{mv^2}{r}\Rightarrow v=\sqrt{\dfrac{GM}{r}}$, which decreases as $r$ increases, while $T=2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{r^3}{GM}}$ increases.

subject: physics
question: Two satellites orbit the Earth in circles of radii $r$ and $4r$. The ratio of their speeds $v_1:v_2$ is
explanation: $v=\sqrt{GM/r}$, so $\dfrac{v_1}{v_2}=\sqrt{\dfrac{4r}{r}}=2$. Ratio $2:1$.

subject: physics
question: The acceleration due to gravity at the Earth's surface is $g$. At a height equal to the Earth's radius $R$ above the surface it is
explanation: $g\propto\dfrac1{r^2}$ and the distance from the centre doubles ($R\to2R$), so $g'=\dfrac g4$.

subject: physics
question: The first cosmic velocity (minimum launch speed for a circular orbit just above the Earth's surface) is about
explanation: $v_1=\sqrt{gR}\approx\sqrt{9.8\times6.4\times10^6}\approx7.9$ km/s. $11.2$ km/s is the escape velocity and $16.7$ km/s the third cosmic velocity.

subject: physics
question: Using $G=6.67\times10^{-11}\ \text{N}\cdot\text{m}^2/\text{kg}^2$, Earth mass $M=6.0\times10^{24}$ kg and radius $R=6.4\times10^6$ m, the gravitational acceleration at the Earth's surface is closest to

subject: physics
question: A geostationary satellite has
options: any orbit with a period of 24 hours
a period of 24 hours and an orbit above the equator
explanation: To stay above the same point, the satellite must turn with the Earth (period $\approx24$ h) in the equatorial plane, which fixes its height too.

subject: physics
question: Two points $A$ and $B$ are on a rotating disc at distances $0.1$ m and $0.3$ m from the axis. The ratio of their linear speeds $v_A:v_B$ is
explanation: Points on the same rigid disc have the same angular velocity $\omega$, and $v=\omega r$, so $v_A:v_B=0.1:0.3=1:3$.

subject: physics
question: A planet has twice the Earth's mass and twice its radius. If the gravitational acceleration on Earth is $10\ \text{m/s}^2$, on the planet it is

subject: physics
question: A wave has frequency $50$ Hz and wavelength $2$ m. Its speed is
explanation: $v=f\lambda=50\times2=100$ m/s.

subject: physics
question: A simple pendulum makes $20$ complete oscillations in $40$ s. Its period is
explanation: $T=\dfrac{\text{time}}{\text{number of oscillations}}=\dfrac{40}{20}=2$ s.

subject: physics
question: The period of a simple pendulum is $T$. If its length is made $4$ times as long, the period becomes
explanation: $T=2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac Lg}\propto\sqrt L$, so $T'=\sqrt4\,T=2T$. The mass of the bob does not matter.

subject: physics
question: A mass of $0.4$ kg on a spring of constant $40$ N/m oscillates. Its period is
explanation: $T=2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac mk}=2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{0.4}{40}}=2\pi\times0.1=\dfrac\pi5\approx0.63$ s.

subject: physics
question: In simple harmonic motion, the speed of the oscillating object is greatest
options: halfway between equilibrium and maximum displacement
explanation: At the equilibrium position all the energy is kinetic, so the speed is maximum (and the restoring force and acceleration are zero). At maximum displacement the speed is zero.

subject: physics
question: In a transverse wave, the particles of the medium vibrate
options: parallel to the direction the wave travels
perpendicular to the direction the wave travels
they move along with the wave
explanation: Transverse: vibration ⟂ propagation (e.g. waves on a string). Longitudinal (e.g. sound): vibration ∥ propagation. In both cases the particles oscillate about fixed positions; only energy travels.

subject: physics
question: Sound travels at $340$ m/s in air. A tuning fork of frequency $680$ Hz produces sound of wavelength
explanation: $\lambda=\dfrac vf=\dfrac{340}{680}=0.5$ m.

subject: physics
question: An object performs SHM described by $x=0.05\sin(4\pi t)$ (SI units). Its amplitude and frequency are
explanation: Compare with $x=A\sin(\omega t)$: $A=0.05$ m and $\omega=4\pi$ rad/s, so $f=\dfrac{\omega}{2\pi}=2$ Hz.

subject: physics
question: A wave travels along a string at $4$ m/s. Two adjacent crests are $0.8$ m apart. The time for a particle on the string to make one full oscillation is
explanation: Adjacent crests are one wavelength apart: $\lambda=0.8$ m. $f=\dfrac v\lambda=5$ Hz, so the period is $T=\dfrac1f=0.2$ s.

subject: physics
question: When a wave passes from one medium into another, the quantity that stays the same is the
explanation: The frequency is set by the source, so it does not change at a boundary. The speed changes with the medium, and so does $\lambda=v/f$.

subject: physics
question: Resonance occurs when
options: the driving frequency equals the natural frequency of the system
explanation: A system driven at its natural frequency absorbs energy most efficiently, so its amplitude becomes very large. This is resonance.

subject: physics
question: A spring oscillator has amplitude $0.1$ m and maximum speed $2$ m/s. Its angular frequency is
explanation: In SHM $v_{\max}=A\omega$, so $\omega=\dfrac{2}{0.1}=20$ rad/s.
